mathematical_review.finding: topMobius uses the actual rational incidence inverse. The interval identity gives a pointwise indicator; exchanging finite sums gives the tested-subset count. No inverse identity is assumed as a free hypothesis.

The exact-top set is a genuine SubMulAction. Its fixed-point subtype is explicitly equivalent to the ambient fixed/exact-support conjunction. Burnside is applied to that actual action; the finite group order is nonzero. Proper support sublevels need not be invariant.

Base equivariance proves fiber stability under the actual base stabilizer. Explicit subtype equivalences identify the fixed/sublevel conditions used in the summand, without replacing them by an abstract counting axiom.

The sigma map sends each actual stabilizer-fiber quotient to its ambient orbit. Base equivariance proves fiber injectivity, orbit separation identifies the sigma index, and representative coverage gives surjectivity. No finiteness or faithfulness is used for this equivalence.
An explicit equivariant subtype swap commutes the support and base restrictions. Nat.card of the resulting sigma is the sum of the actual fiber orbit cardinalities, yielding UD.AdmissibleExtensions.

Quotient representatives satisfy coverage and separation in Lean. All E-orbits may be indexed because empty fibers contribute zero. The arbitrary-transversal theorem permits exactly one representative of each orbit in p(R), as in the manuscript.

An order isomorphism fixes top. A family of order isomorphisms plus the stated support equivariance suffices; the manuscript group action supplies these hypotheses. The theorem is slightly more general and assumes neither the bijection nor its counting conclusion.
